level: Level 2R — the Level-2 94.48M hybrid on real public-domain English
question: Can this hybrid DeltaNet/attention architecture at 94.48M parameters learn meaningful natural-language structure from real English?
answer: Yes, partially. It learns non-trivial natural-language structure and avoids Level 2's catastrophic unigram-style collapse. Its generation remains repetitive and semantically weak at this scale.
git_commit_note: not recorded in the committed artifacts; the checkpoint's metadata.json on persistent storage carries the commit the run was launched from

hardware.estimate_source: qwen_distill.diagnostics.fit.estimate_training_memory at seq 1024, batch 4, gradient checkpointing on, fp16
hardware.estimate_vs_outcome: the run completed without OOM on a 14.56 GiB card, so 3.57 GiB is not an over-prediction; peak usage was not measured

configuration.parameters_measured_note: count_parameters on the rebuilt spec; 94.48M is that figure rounded
configuration.corpus: real public-domain English (Project Gutenberg), document-level split

corpus.split_rule: document level — whole works to train or validation, never both
corpus.committed_to_git_note: corpus text is never committed; regenerate with scripts/prepare_level2r_dataset.py and verify with scripts/verify_corpus.py against the digest above

training_measurements.run_wide_note: 32,768,000 tokens / 18,963.8 s. This is the run-wide scope and it INCLUDES validation passes, checkpoint writes and ten verified Drive persists. It is not the interval rate.
training_measurements.interval_note: ~2.1k tok/s observed at the console between log records — CORROBORATED, not read from a log file by this analysis. The gap to the run-wide figure is non-training overhead.
training_measurements.metrics_jsonl_note: metrics.jsonl and summary.json live on persistent storage with the checkpoints and are not committed. The trajectory above is the authoritative record supplied with the run.

train_validation_gap.trend: stable, not widening — no overfitting signal at this token budget

learning_rate_at_final_block.note: OneCycleLR(max_lr=6e-4, total_steps=2000) reaches ~0 by step 2000. The final block ran at 0.9% of peak LR.

saturation_reasoning: the run saw 0.826 epochs; 17.4% of the training corpus was never read
the final blocks' flattening is confounded with the LR schedule reaching ~0 by construction — at 0.9% of peak LR the model was barely being updated
validation decreased monotonically through the last block; nothing plateaued or turned
the train/validation gap is stable, so the limit is not overfitting
these are three independent reasons the 2000-step horizon was a budget, not an endpoint
trajectory_analysis.horizon_verdict: 2000 steps is a CONTROLLED BASELINE, not a scientific endpoint
trajectory_analysis.contrast_with_level2: Level 2 flattened because it had consumed its 8 MB corpus 4.1 times over. Level 2R flattened because its learning rate ran out with 17.4% of the corpus unread. The curves look similar and the causes are opposite.

observed_failure_modes: phrase-level repetition ('the street was standing before the street was standing before')
clause-level looping ('the stranger was still and the stranger was still')
motif lock-in on a small set of nouns: stranger, street, thing, man, property, service
sanity_generation.detector_limitation: the degeneracy thresholds are calibrated for Level 2's single-token collapse (>50% one token, <15% distinct words, a repeating character cycle). Phrase-level repetition clears all three, so 0/11 degenerate means 'not collapsed', not 'not repetitive'.

model_quality.interpretation: The 94.48M hybrid learns non-trivial natural-language structure from real English and avoids catastrophic unigram-style collapse, but its generation remains repetitive and semantically weak at this scale.

model_quality.greedy_generations_source: verbatim from sanity.json — the authoritative record; greedy, 96 new tokens, prompt set v2.0

establishes: the hybrid DeltaNet/attention architecture at 94.48M learns non-trivial natural-language structure from real English
it avoids Level 2's catastrophic 'and and and' unigram collapse under an otherwise identical setup
real English word forms, function-word placement and local grammatical structure are produced
no verbatim memorisation of the training corpus was detected at 96-token greedy generation
the checkpoint/resume/verified-persistence stack works end to end across ten checkpoints
the analytical memory estimate of 3.57 GiB was not an over-prediction on a 14.56 GiB T4
~1,728 tok/s run-wide at 94.48M on a T4 with real-corpus I/O, validation and verified Drive persistence
does_not_establish: that the model is fluent, useful, instruction-following, benchmark-competitive or teacher-equivalent
that 94.48M is a sufficient or appropriate size for anything
that the validation curve had converged — the run ended with the learning rate at ~0 and 17.4% of the corpus unread
that a larger model would do better, which is what Level 3 exists to test
anything about distillation, knowledge transfer or the teacher
that validation BPB 1.797 is comparable to Level 2's 1.270 — different corpora, different intrinsic entropy, no delta is meaningful
unknown: peak VRAM actually used (never measured; only the 3.57 GiB estimate exists)
the git commit the run was launched from
where the validation curve would go with a longer horizon or a schedule matched to a longer horizon
whether the repetition is a capacity limit, a data-budget limit, or a decoding artefact of greedy search
